articles.title: High mortgage rates are deepening a ‘K-shaped’ housing market
articles.summary: In today’s housing market, there is a growing divide between the “haves” and the “have-nots.”
articles.body: In today’s housing market, there is a growing divide between the “haves” and the “have-nots.” The typical homebuyer faces mounting affordability challenges as home prices rise and inventory remains limited. Adding to the pressure: The recent surge in mortgage rates is making the decision to buy a home even more difficult for many, deepening affordability challenges The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.4% this week, according to data released Thursday by Freddie Mac. That’s a significant jump from this time last year, when the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 6.27%. With the US midterm elections just weeks away, rising mortgage rates are adding fresh pressure to an already strained housing market at a time when affordability issues are a key concern for many voters. Higher-income buyers, buoyed by more cash on hand and larger budgets, are accounting for a growing share of the housing market, while lower-income buyers struggle to keep up. It’s a divide that reflects the broader “K-shaped” economy: as the cost of living rises, wealthier Americans are better positioned to absorb the hit, while those with tighter budgets have less room to spare. The same split is playing out in the housing market: Americans who are less sensitive to higher interest rates increasingly have the upper hand. “It’s very expensive to get into a house if you’re looking for one right now,” said Oscar Munoz, head of US economics at TD Securities. “The only people that we find are driving transactions in the housing market are high-income consumers.” “They have the wealth to transact in this market, which is unaffordable for most Americans,” Munoz added. Data from TD Securities, commissioned by Morning Consult, shows a growing divergence in homebuying intentions this year. After tracking broadly with other income groups for several years, Americans earning $100,000 or more are now increasingly likely to say they want to buy a home, compared to lower-income consumers. The recent rise in mortgage rates above 7% may widen the gap, Munoz said, as higher monthly payments make it harder for lower-income Americans to qualify for a mortgage or afford the payments if they do. Higher-end buyers are likely also benefiting from a strong stock market, which hit record highs as recently as last week, giving them more purchasing power. “There are different markets by geography, different markets by price point. What we’re seeing is the low end is dragging down the overall market,” Compass CEO Robert Reffkin said of a slowdown in home sales in an appearance on CNBC last month. Rate-sensitive buyers getting spooked In Los Angeles, Brock and Lori Harris, a husband-and-wife real estate team, said buyers whose budgets are stretched by the prospect of higher mortgage payments have begun stepping back from the market. “I always find it funny that cars are marketed as a monthly payment, but homes are not. Homes just show the price and then you have to pull out your mortgage calculator to figure out what your payment is,” said Brock Harris. “And suddenly, that payment is much, much higher than it used to be.” National data points to a pullback from home shoppers who need to borrow money to afford a home. Mortgage applications last week were 16% lower than the same week one year ago, according to data the Mortgage Bankers Association released Wednesday. Brock and Lori Harris said they’re seeing more cash buyers in the market in LA, but even those buyers are keeping a tighter grip on their wallets than they did just a few years ago. “They’re aware, but they’re less sensitive to interest rates,” Lori Harris said of cash buyers. “Whereas a buyer who is taking out a loan might be priced out of a house they qualified to buy just two or three months ago because of these high rates.” Nationally, cash sales accounted for 27% of transactions in September, according to the National Association of Realtors’ latest data released Tuesday. That is down from 30% a year ago, but mortgage rates didn’t breach 7% until the final week of September, crossing a threshold that some experts say could make buyers who rely on mortgage loans hit pause. Mortgage rates tend to track bond yields, which have been volatile in recent months as investors anticipate further Federal Reserve rate hikes to rein in inflation. Those expectations have pushed bond yields higher, putting upward pressure on mortgage rates. In the weeks after mortgage rates crossed 7% late last month, eXp Realty, one of the country’s largest real estate brokerages, saw a higher-than-usual deal cancellation rate, said Leo Pareja, the CEO of AGNT, the parent company of eXp Realty. “What that tells us is that it is shocking psychologically. It’s a real barrier,” Pareja told CNN, though he added that the deal cancellation rate has since returned to normal levels for this time of year. For home shoppers still hunting for affordability in this higher interest rate environment, Pareja advised looking at new construction. New homes have traditionally commanded a price premium over existing homes, but that relationship has flipped over the past two years. Existing home prices rose 1.3% year over year in September to $417,500, marking 39 consecutive months of annual gains, according to NAR. Meanwhile, the median price of a new home was $393,700 in August, according to the latest Census Bureau data. “Unlike a homeowner who tests the market and doesn’t get their price, they can just pull it off the market if they have a lower interest rate… but a builder is in the business of selling,” Pareja said. As a result, builders are leaning more heavily on incentives to attract new buyers, including mortgage rate buydowns that can help lower monthly payments, Pareja said.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addresses CoreWeave stock plunge: 'I'm optimistic'

Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang addressed the recent discord at key partner and fallen AI stock darling CoreWeave ( CRWV ) on Thursday, expressing optimism in the data center operator following a 15% rout on Wednesday and a smaller dip on Thursday morning.

"CoreWeave's strength is improving every day," Huang shared at a Bloomberg event in Stockholm. "I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing." His input was much anticipated this week as concerns about the health of CoreWeave and its exposures to Nvidia have continued to build.

Huang's need to weigh in wasn't a surprise to veteran tech analyst Tal Liani, who just this morning published a bullish note on CoreWeave with an aggressive $140 price target . "Don't forget that Nvidia is basically financing all these deals with them, with other hyperscalers because they want to block off the competition. They want to make sure that CoreWeave and others are using Nvidia GPUs and not AMD GPUs," Liani said on Sozzi Unleashed .

Liani added, "So at the end of the day, there is an inherent interest both ways. And I'm sure that you're going to hear from everyone on the planet that has a vested interest in the build-out of data centers. You're going to hear comforting kinds of comments about the validity of the demand and the sustainability of the demand, including Jensen. It's just a question of time."

In January of this year, Nvidia announced an expansion of its relationship with CoreWeave. The deal included Nvidia investing $2 billion in CoreWeave stock . CoreWeave committed to using Nvidia's technology to build more than 5 gigawatts of AI factories by 2030.

Nvidia now holds 47.2 million shares of CoreWeave stock, or around 10% of the company.

(Bloomberg) -- Iambic Therapeutics Inc. shares soared 16% in its trading debut after the clinical-stage cancer drugmaker and technology firm raised $150 million in a US initial public offering.

The biotech's shares traded at $18.50 each as of 12:21 p.m. in New York on Thursday after being paused for volatility, above its IPO price of $16 apiece.

The trading gives the firm, which counts Nvidia Corp. as a shareholder, a market value of $877 million, based on the outstanding shares.

The San Diego-based firm uses AI and machine learning to help it discover new treatments, the filing shows. Iambic will use the proceeds from the IPO to advance three early-stage cancer drug candidates.

ARK Investment Management, which is already an investor in Iambic, and billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office had expressed an interest in buying as much as $60 million worth of shares in the offering in aggregate.

The oncology-focused firm is poised to capitalize on investor excitement about the potential for artificial intelligence to speed up biological discoveries.

The San Diego-based firm partnered with Abbvie Inc. to accelerate AI-enabled drug discovery in immunology, neuroscience and oncology, and has relationships with drugmakers such as Takeda Pharmaceutical Co. and H. Lundbeck A/S, the filing showed. Iambic also counts Nvidia and AI cloud firm Lambda Inc. among its partners.

The drugmaker had a net loss of $50.1 million on revenue of $12.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, versus a net loss of $33.2 million on revenue of $3.9 million for the corresponding period a year before, a previous filing showed.

Iambic has raised $461.8 million from both technology and healthcare-focused investors since the firm was founded in 2019. Catalio Capital Management's stake is expected to fall to 8.9% after the offering from 11%, while Nexus Venture Partners will have 6.8%, down from 8.5%, according to the filing. Nvidia participated in several of Iambic's convertible preferred stock financings, the filing shows.

The offering was led by JPMorgan Chase & Co., Jefferies Financial Group Inc., Bank of America Corp. and Citigroup Inc. The company trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol IAM.

articles.title: AI trade rout sparks flight to Treasurys, bond yields sink: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Investors flocked to safety as the AI trade has unwound over the past two sessions.
articles.body:
A sell-off in the AI trade has fueled investor interest in Treasurys, driving dramatic swings in bond yields.

The 10-year Treasury ( ^TNX ) yield, used as a benchmark for mortgages and other loans, sank 14 basis points to 5.05%. The 30-year yield (^ TYX ) also tumbled 13 basis points to 5.40%, as seen on Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace chart below.

A global sell-off in chip stocks , exacerbated by AI financing worries , pushed investors toward Treasurys. Bond yields extended declines after reversing their gains on Wednesday following a hotter-than-expected inflation report.

The two-day action in bond yields could be a precursor to the road ahead if AI spending were to decelerate.

"It would weaken the USD and reduce US yields across the curve," wrote Thierry Wizman, global FX & rates strategist at Macquarie Group.

"That's because it would mark the end of superlative US growth against the rest of the developed economies," he said.

Bond yields have hit the highest levels in more than 20 years , raising concerns about higher borrowing costs and their impact on the broader stock market.

Sticky inflation has also led strategists to price in at least another rate hike this year. However, as of Thursday morning, market participants have raised their probability to 72% that Federal Reserve officials will hold rates steady at their policy meeting this month.

Macquarie Group strategists, along with UBS and Goldman Sachs analysts, see a Fed pause in October, followed by a rate hike at the Fed's December meeting.

articles.title: Rocket Lab stock tumbles as effort to take market share from SpaceX slips to 2027
articles.summary: Rocket Lab stock tumbled on Thursday after the space company said the first launch of Neutron, its reusable medium-lift rocket, slipped to 2027.
articles.body:
Rocket Lab ( RKLB ) stock tumbled more than 10% on Thursday after the space company said the first launch of Neutron, its reusable medium-lift rocket, slipped to 2027.

Rocket Lab had targeted the fourth quarter of 2026 for Neutron's debut. CEO Peter Beck blamed manufacturing issues in the forward propellant dome on the rocket's first stage.

"They don't necessarily mean that the dome would fail on flight, but our practice is to proceed only when we believe the system has the appropriate margins," Beck said in a video update, according to Stocktwits. "Possible success isn't our standard."

Beck said the company has identified manufacturing fixes and expects to finish assembling the first stage within the quarter, when it will be in a better position to announce a launch date. He also pointed to strong demand and upcoming contract announcements.

Neutron is central to Rocket Lab's effort to compete for larger missions in a market dominated by SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Falcon 9. Its schedule has slipped before: Rocket Lab unveiled the rocket in 2021 with a 2024 first-flight target, then moved it to mid-2025 and then to 2026. A first-stage tank ruptured during testing in January.

The plunge came after a 7.9% drop in Wednesday's regular session, before Rocket Lab released the update at 4:40 p.m. ET.

If Thursday's drop holds through the close, it would be Rocket Lab's lowest close since December 2025. The stock is down around 25% this year and about 65% below its 52-week high of $151, set in May.

Space stocks were already under pressure. AST SpaceMobile ( ASTS ) fell 10% Wednesday after Piper Sandler cut its price target to $54, citing competition from SpaceX.

Rocket Lab is also working to close its deal for satellite operator Iridium ( IRDM ).

Cantor Fitzgerald kept its Overweight rating and $122 price target on Rocket Lab after the update, according to Yahoo Finance analyst data.

articles.title: He bought a home, gave it for redevelopment years later and sold new flat for Rs 1.95 crore within 8 days; taxman denied LTCG exemption and added Rs 80.14 lakh, but ITAT grants relief
articles.summary: You buy a flat and after some years the housing society gives it for redevelopment.
articles.body: You buy a flat and after some years the housing society gives it for redevelopment. You then sell the redeveloped flat within days of getting it and claim long-term capital gains exemption.But the Income Tax Department treats these as two different transactions and applies short-term capital gains tax. What do you do?In one such case a man faced a tax notice and subsequently had to appeal before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), where he won relief.What the case is about The man had purchased a 510-square-foot flat in a housing society in Mumbai, during FY 2006-07, where he lived with his wife. Many years later, in FY 2012-13, the housing society entered into a redevelopment agreement with a builder. Under the arrangement, the man was allotted a replacement flat in the same society. This flat had 30% more area than his original home.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleThe builder handed over the redeveloped flat to the man after the two parties entered into an Agreement for Permanent Alternate Accommodation in 2018.However, eight days after signing the agreement, the man sold the redeveloped flat for Rs 1.95 crore.On his part, he classified the profit from this transaction as long-term capital gains (LTCG) and sought a tax exemption under Section 54F.The man said that he had invested the entire Rs 1.95 crore from the sale in purchasing another residential flat at a different location, making him eligible for the exemption.However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) took a different view. According to the AO, the transfer of the original flat to the developer under the redevelopment arrangement and the subsequent sale of the redeveloped flat were actually two separate transactions.With this view, the AO classified the gains as short-term capital gains (STCG), and denied the man the Section 54F exemption. This made the proceeds from the Rs 1.95 crore sale taxable. He also disallowed the benefit of indexation.The AO added Rs 80.14 lakh to the man’s taxable income, which was 50% share of the short-term capital gains.Also Read | Medicine shop owner deposited Rs 2.47 crore cash, faced unexplained money tax notice; ITAT Delhi says Income Tax Dept could not counter his evidence, rules in his favourThe Commissioner of Appeals also upheld the AO’s assessment. The appellate authority observed that the arrangement could not be treated as a straightforward sale and purchase.Instead, it involved the transfer of rights in the original flat, followed by the allotment of a newly constructed, substantially larger property under the redevelopment scheme.The man challenged the order before ITAT Mumbai. On July 16, 2026, the tribunal ruled in his favour.Why did the homeowner win the case?Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that ITAT Mumbai considered the redeveloped flat to be a continuation or substitution of the ownership rights associated with the original property.The tribunal held that such a property is not necessarily a new capital asset acquired only upon the execution of the Permanent Alternate Accommodation Agreement (PAAA).Under the redevelopment arrangement entered into by the housing society and accepted by the man, he was entitled to permanent alternate accommodation that included the area of his original flat, an additional 30% in carpet area at no cost, 185 square feet transferred by his mother and another 55 square feet purchased from the developer for Rs 6 lakh.The tribunal also ruled that the various portions of the redeveloped flat could not be treated as separate capital assets simply because the man received additional space or purchased extra area as part of the redevelopment arrangement.Also Read | Homebuyer paid Rs 91 lakh upfront for a Rs 1.24 crore property, but circle value rose to Rs 1.46 crore by registration; why ITAT Kolkata gave her tax relief and deleted Rs 11.35 lakh additionThe AO had accepted that Section 56(2)(x) did not apply to the transaction, since the man received the redeveloped flat under the redevelopment arrangement. The payment of Rs 6 lakh was considered to relate only to the additional area he had purchased.For calculating the capital gains, however, the AO treated the redeveloped flat as a separate asset acquired afresh on the date the Permanent Alternate Accommodation Agreement (PAAA) was signed. Since the man sold the property just eight days later, the resulting profit was classified as short-term capital gains (STCG).ITAT Mumbai rejected this interpretation, observing that redevelopment does not generally terminate an existing owner's property rights and replace them with ownership of an entirely new asset.Explaining the reasoning, Surana said: “Instead, the ownership rights continue throughout the redevelopment process and are substituted from the old premises to the newly constructed premises.”According to this interpretation, the PAAA only recorded and specified the permanent alternate accommodation that the taxpayer was already entitled to receive under the development agreement. It did not establish his ownership rights for the first time.Also Read |Man jointly bought Rs 80 lakh property with father and wife but didn't file ITR; taxman added Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained money, but ITAT grants relief after proof of family contributionsSurana said: “Accordingly, the execution date of the PAAA could not be regarded as the starting point for computing the holding period.”The tribunal further clarified that the holding period must be calculated from the date on which the taxpayer acquired enforceable rights over the property, rather than the subsequent execution of the PAAA or a conveyance document. In this case, those rights originated in 2006 and remained in place throughout the redevelopment process.ITAT also considered an alternative calculation based on the development agreement dated February 15, 2013. Even if the holding period were counted from that date, the man had held the property for nearly five years before selling it on January 20, 2018. This was well beyond the prescribed 24-month period.ITAT Mumbai treated the gains of Rs 1.95 crore as long-term capital gains, allowed relief under Section 54/54F and set aside the Rs 80.14 lakh income tax addition.Also Read | Mother nominated son for savings account, but both died; Farmer father faced long delays, got money but lodged a compliant, Consumer Commission orders bank to pay Rs 15,000 reliefYou use AI every day. articles.title: The Fed still has little control over the 2 biggest inflation drivers
articles.summary: While the CPI inflation report for September increased the chances for a Fed hike, ING's James Knightley argues that the central bank has little control over...
articles.body:
Wednesday morning's inflation data put a late-October Fed hike squarely on the table, raising the chances of a hike from around 22% to 54%, according to the CME's Fed futures market.

Surging gas prices have been a particular pain for consumers, and they were the major driver for September's price acceleration from August and the 3.7% year-over-year inflation reading.

That expensive oil, coupled with the expensive AI data center build-outs, has delivered the highest year-over-year figure since 2023.

While the Fed often favors "core" inflation readings, which exclude volatile food and energy prices to better show the overall economic picture, expensive gas and diesel have been around long enough that they're now baked into the prices of everything else.

Plus, as former Chair Jerome Powell would consistently note , families can't strip out food and energy costs.

Even before Wednesday's hot inflation data, we've been hearing from Fed officials who see higher rates as necessary to chill the economy, so it's not surprising to see markets shift their predictions.

But as ING economist James Knightley wrote in a note to clients, "rate hikes will have limited impact on these two price drivers."

"In terms of the outlook for inflation, much hinges on what happens with the Strait of Hormuz," Knightley added.

The ball, Knightley notes, is out of the Fed's hands, given that it has no foreign policy control and its high rates are no match for hyperscaler enthusiasm.

But the ING economist did give us all something else to watch, something that's already working in ways the Fed might want to cool the economy: flagging wages.

With almost no labor market turnover, wage growth is in the dumps at just 3% — less than inflation, we might add.

"The key story ... is wage growth, which is the biggest cost input for corporate America," Knightley noted.

While the low levels are "bad news for households," he added, "this will help to dampen price pressures over the medium to longer term."

Thursday's retail sales reading and wholesale price inflation gauge may not move the needle, meaning that we may be set to go into another Fed meeting on the edge of our seats, yet again.

Ethan Wolff-Mann is a Senior Editor at Yahoo Finance, running newsletters. Follow him on X @ewolffmann .

articles.title: OpenAI plans Hindi-tuned voice model
articles.summary: OpenAI to launch Hindi-tuned voice model for ChatGPT, exploring India-first features for Android, mixed Hindi-English use and intermittent internet connectivity.
articles.body: Bengaluru: OpenAI will roll out a Hindi-tuned voice model for ChatGPT and is exploring a differentiated experience tailored to India’s languages, Android phones and intermittent internet connectivity as it seeks to expand adoption in the country.Vijaye Raji, OpenAI’s chief technology officer of applications, said India’s preference for voice interactions was shaping its product priorities. “To be accessible and used in India, we need to focus on voice,” Raji said on the sidelines of the AI giant’s developer event in Bengaluru.Raji grew up in Puducherry and moved to the US around 25 years ago. He spent nearly two decades at Microsoft and Facebook before founding Statsig, a platform that helps companies test and improve their products. He joined OpenAI following its acquisition of Statsig in 2025 and now oversees product engineering for ChatGPT and Codex.The company said its upcoming GPT-Live 1.1 would initially roll out in the ChatGPT app with two native Hindi voices designed to make conversations sound more natural. Raji described it as a Hindi-tuned model, distinguishing it from ChatGPT’s existing ability to converse in Indian languages.“One of the things I want to explore is a differentiated experience for India,” he said. “This is an Android-first market. We want to be able to take the native Android experiences and build that into the product.”Raji said teams were learning from users who mix Hindi and English within the same session and use voice notes. Ensuring products remain reliable when internet connectivity is intermittent is another consideration. “It’s not enough that we build all these capable products. We want to make them usable,” he said.OpenAI executives said the number of people using ChatGPT in India had doubled from a year earlier, though they did not disclose the current user base. Raji said he expected further growth and investment in the country.Raji, who oversees advertising and growth alongside the technology underpinning ChatGPT and Codex, said advertising helps fund free access and support wider adoption.“We want to grow, and growth comes from providing affordable and accessible services,” he said. OpenAI recently introduced advertising in India, giving businesses another way to reach users through the platform.Raji said the company had priced its lower-cost ChatGPT Go subscription specifically for India rather than simply converting dollar prices into rupees. The plan aims to lower the cost of accessing more capable models. Education is among the major uses of ChatGPT in India, company executives have said.OpenAI is also seeking to connect its consumer, enterprise and developer businesses. Raji said developers could use ChatGPT to reach its audience, while enterprises were deploying the company’s technology in services such as customer support and voice agents.Expanding support for Indian languages will depend partly on access to training data, Raji said. OpenAI’s data teams work with partners to obtain properly licensed content for model training, he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Will the Fed raise interest rates this month? A Kevin Warsh speech could offer clues
articles.summary: When Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh strides onstage in Bangkok on Friday morning, it will be after 11 p.m. on Thursday in New York.
articles.body: When Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh strides onstage in Bangkok on Friday morning, it will be after 11 p.m. on Thursday in New York. But investors, economists and politicians in the United States will be awake and hanging on his every word. Any speech by a Fed chair is closely scrutinized. This week’s talk has an extra dose of urgency, though, after two government reports showed inflation heating up for consumers and businesses — spurring speculation about how soon the Fed will raise interest rates to handle soaring prices. Warsh will be speaking at the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, where he will be interviewed by IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva. The Fed chairman has repeatedly said he will not use public speaking engagements to intentionally steer the expectations of investors and markets, but his comments could nevertheless signal whether the central bank will hike rates before, or after, the Nov. 3 midterm elections. It will also be the last speech from a Fed official before policymakers enter a “blackout” period on Saturday that lasts through their next interest rate meeting, which is scheduled for Oct. 27 and 28. “Broad based” inflation “strengthens the case for an October hike,” Bank of America analysts wrote on Wednesday. “The data continue to underscore two key sources of inflation pressure: AI and Iran.” Those two factors aren’t likely to be going anywhere soon, either. The price of politics Already hammered by soaring interest rates, rising energy prices and stagnant wage growth, American consumers could get an extra dose of financial strain if the Fed raises rates again this month. Voters are already dissatisfied with President Donald Trump’s handling of the economy, polls show, so another rate hike could add to Republicans’ headaches as they face potentially losing their congressional majorities in the midterms. In recent weeks, Trump has tried to pull multiple policy levers to lower gas and diesel prices, which have pushed inflation higher in recent months. But none of them have yet slowed prices meaningfully. “Starting on day one, we will end inflation and make America affordable again,” Trump said on the campaign trail in 2024. Inflation as measured by the consumer price index declined to as low as 2.3% four months into Trump’s term. But that same month, Trump unleashed a wave of tariffs across the globe, dramatically changing the economic story. By September, inflation breached the 3% threshold again. In February, Trump launched the war against Iran, causing one of the worst energy supply shocks in history. Inflation jumped as high as 4.1% in May, and looks to be headed back in that direction again. Another Fed rate hike would also further undermine Trump’s yearslong pressure campaign to push the central bank to cut rates. Since Warsh took his post in May, the central bank has either held rates steady or increased them. Trump hasn’t attacked Warsh after years of hammering former Chair Jerome Powell. But the president has started saying that the other members of the Fed’s board are “very hostile.” “I’m relying on Kevin,” Trump told reporters in September, “but he’s got, you know, a very tough board. He’s got a board that was put there by a lot of other people, and the interest rates are too high.” “They’re very political,” Trump said. Four of the Fed’s seven board members were appointed by Trump. Asked what the president’s expectations are for Warsh’s appearance, the White House pointed to a Truth Social post from September in which Trump had written, “Interest rates in the United States should be 1% or less.” Diesel and the damage done Economists and investors are paying close attention to so-called core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices. Both reports this week showed that even this adjusted measure of price growth is running hotter than hoped for. “Core CPI was the more significant surprise,” wrote analysts at Bank of America. The core readings showed that skyrocketing fuel prices, particularly diesel, are trickling down. Farmers, truckers and others who keep commerce humming in the United States have to raise their prices in order to digest higher diesel costs. That, in turn, leads to price increases for consumer goods. “The cost of diesel gets into just about everything,” KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk told NBC News in an August interview. “Everything from … running a farm … cost of food, but also everything across the economy that’s shipped gets that extra fee tacked onto it.” At the time, she described the surge in diesel fuel prices as likely “an inflationary problem for the next several months.” Her warning came to fruition in September, according to the consumer price index and producer price index reports this week. With diesel prices remaining solidly above $6 per gallon so far in October, and with no sign that the Iran war is near an end or that attacks on energy assets in the Ukraine-Russia war will be paused, it could keep fueling overall inflation for months. Big Tech is also fueling inflation. Trillion-dollar companies are spending, and borrowing, big sums for servers, memory and other components that will be used in data centers. That’s caused price spikes across the economy. Companies including Apple and Nintendo have raised prices as a result. “We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly,” Apple told NBC News in June. Companies are also tapping the public debt markets in an unprecedented way. Data center companies and associated utility firms, chipmakers and cloud providers are expected to raise between $300 billion and $570 billion from the debt market this year, according to Vanguard. Those firms are also offering highly attractive interest rates, sometimes better than U.S. Treasury bonds. A consequence of that, Warsh noted recently, is that there’s a “competition for capital” driving up interest rates on government debt, too. “This is a complicated set of things that are affecting the most important asset anywhere in the world, the 10-year Treasury,” Warsh said. “It’s the risk-free asset upon which every price of virtually every asset in the world is related to.” Without referencing the Iran war, he also said yields were being driven by “geopolitics” and the strength of the economy.

articles.title: Housing stocks are the AI sell-off's winners as bond yields sink
articles.summary: Despite ongoing pressure in the tech sector, housing-related companies saw a bounce on Thursday.
articles.body:
Housing stocks have turned out to be a surprise winner in the tech stock sell-off. Despite ongoing pressure in the tech sector, listings giant Zillow ( Z ) gained 11% on Thursday. Homebuying and selling platform Opendoor ( OPEN ) surged 17%, online brokerage Compass ( COMP ) jumped nearly 10%, and commercial real estate database CoStar ( CSGP ) rose more than 6%. The reason for their success has to do with the close relationship between mortgage rates and bond yields. Lately, investors have been shunning US government debt, sending yields and mortgage rates sharply higher. But on Thursday, the sell-off in chip stocks sent investors fleeing back to their classic safe-haven investment, Treasurys . Because bond prices and yields move inversely, yields on long-dated government debt dropped sharply. The drop in yields is a sign that home financing costs could get a breather after a bruising few weeks that sent mortgage rates to around 7.5%. The 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates closely track, was down 10 basis points Thursday afternoon. That translated to a 12-basis-point drop in average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rates to 7.33%, according to Mortgage News Daily. Last week, rates averaged 7.4% , according to Freddie Mac data, near a three-year high. Despite Thursday's enthusiasm, it's been a bruising time to invest in housing-linked stocks. The housing market has been nearly frozen for more than three years, hurting the companies' bottom lines and battering their share prices. Shares of Zillow are down 67% over the last five years, while Opendoor has lost 90% of its value in the same time period.

Claire Boston is a Senior Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: VA disability benefits could increase 3.6% in 2027. Here's what to expect.
articles.summary: VA disability compensation COLA follows the Social Security adjustment. Here’s what the 3.6% COLA in 2027 means for veterans.
articles.body:

Veterans receiving disability benefits are set to see a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in 2027.

Following the Social Security Administration's COLA increase this week, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is set to increase veterans' disability compensation by the same 3.6%. More than 6 million veterans who currently receive disability compensation from the VA will get the increase next year.

Each year, Congress must pass the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act before the VA can make the increase official. The law ties VA disability benefits to the Social Security COLA so beneficiaries can keep pace with inflation.

Now that the SSA has released the 3.6% COLA increase for 2027, the legislation must pass before the VA can make the increase official for beneficiaries. But veterans can still use the confirmed COLA to estimate how their payments will change.

Here's what to know about the 2027 COLA and how VA disability benefits will be affected:

The SSA announced on Oct. 14 that its 2027 COLA for beneficiaries is 3.6% — the largest increase in four years . The COLA amount is based on the Consumer Price Index for urban workers (CPI-W) averages for July, August, and September 2026, compared with the same months in 2025.

If Congress approves, the 3.6% COLA that Social Security beneficiaries receive will also apply to VA disability compensation.

VA disability payments are tax-free, and eligible veterans receive them monthly. Veterans can qualify based on mental or physical conditions that developed before, during, or after they served in the military. That might include conditions that appeared after serving, for example, or existing conditions that were worsened by their service.

Specifically, the COLA increase applies to compensation for wartime disability, compensation for dependents, clothing allowances for eligible disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation (DIC) for surviving spouses and children.

How much will the COLA increase VA benefits in 2027?

The VA hasn't published 2027 compensation benefits rate tables, but beneficiaries can use the current rate tables to estimate their COLA increase for the new year.

The monthly payment that eligible veterans will actually receive in 2027 depends on the specific benefits they qualify for.

For example, take a veteran with a 10% disability rating who currently receives $180.42 in disability compensation. That monthly payment will increase by $6.50 ($180.42 x 0.036) in 2027, for a new monthly total of $186.92.

The higher a veteran's disability compensation is, the more impact they'll see from the COLA increase.

A veteran with an 80% disability rating, for example, who also has one child and a spouse, currently receives $2,406.15 per month. In 2027, that monthly payment will increase by $86.62 ($2,406.15 x 0.036) for a new total of $2,492.77.

Beyond the amounts within the VA's rate table, a family's total VA disability compensation may also be affected by added amounts that they may qualify for. This includes additional children or Aid and Attendance benefits that spouses may receive.

For veterans receiving disability compensation, there's no action to take now.

The 3.6% COLA increase will automatically be applied to monthly payments throughout 2027. You don't need to file a new claim to receive it.

The Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026 — which will finalize the VA's compensation adjustment — has already been introduced into Congress, though it's still waiting to pass into law. Once it's final, the VA will update its current compensation benefits rate tables , and you can see exactly how your monthly payment is affected based on your disability rating and dependents.

The new rate should be effective as of Dec. 1, 2026, though based on payment dates, veterans aren't likely to see the increased amount in their disability compensation until Dec. 31 or even January.
